subject: ventures/asphalt-driveway-pave-bid-calculator
professional: a senior asphalt paving estimator / residential paving contractor; they check tons per square foot at the stated lift first, then how crew labor is built (crew size x hours x loaded wage), then whether demo, millings and base are priced as their own tickets

evidence.correctness: Independent Python model (scratchpad/asphalt/model.py, not the author's code) recomputed four outputs and all match calc.mjs to the cent: 800 sq ft 2 in overlay 9.667 t (145 pcf) vs 9.778 t by the NAPA/DOT 110 lb/sy/in rule (1.1% apart, within normal practice), price $3,076.25; 1,000 sq ft full-depth preset 20.058 t, walk-away $4,701.72, price $6,530.17; failed-base gravel 200 sq ft x 4 in at 135 pcf = 4.50 t (calc baseTons 4.4999); 1,200 sq ft mill-and-overlay $5,073.38; fabric delta $1,905.14 = 2,150 x 0.55 x 1.16 / 0.72. Every README and how-much-page figure ($3,076, $6,530, $5,287, $5,787, $5,073, $10,801, 16.4 t, 11.2 h) reproduces. The arithmetic is right; the labor model's meaning is the problem (domain).
evidence.completeness: Checked: three methods, mix tons, apron lift, failed base, sawcut, fabric, walk-away, method comparison (compareMethods returns overlay 5287 / mill 5787 / full-depth 6530 on the preset), proposed-price check, copy summary, share link, saved bid, printable proposal (proposal.mjs present, 482-line test). Served page https://marisstella.app/asphalt-driveway-pave-bid-calculator/ returns 200 and served llms.txt carries marisstella.app URLs. No stubs or TODOs found. Not modelled (stated in README limitations): night work, traffic control.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs': 149 pass, 0 fail. Nine hand-seeded mutations in calc.mjs (density 145->140, margin divide->markup, hoursBase=0, demoTons on wrong method, fabric on driveway area only, tack hours on full-depth, millings off, apron hours off, failed-base guard disabled): all nine caught. Page figures are pinned to calc.mjs by tests. Held at 3, not 4, because the fabric-page test builds its own copy of the page defaults and omits hoursTrip and siteHours, so it pins the page to numbers the tool never shows (tests-check-a-copy).
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (449 lines), index.html script (readInput/update/applyJob), the fabric-page test. calc.mjs is pure, validated, readable, no dead code. Defect: number() treats a blank string as 0 (Number('') === 0) and the page passes raw field strings, so clearing Crew hourly wage silently prices labor at $0 (price 3,076.25 -> 2,624.50) and clearing Mix cost / ton prices mix free (-> 1,440.97); clearing Existing depth on full-depth silently drops all demo tons (6,530.17 -> 5,951.98). '1,200' and negatives are rejected with a message (good).
evidence.claims: Disclaimer present on every page. Backed: README and how-much-page dollar figures; vs-flat-rate $4,700 / $3,780. Not backed: fabric page table ($8,714.45 / $10,619.59) disagrees with the tool on the same preset ($8,896.28 / $10,801.42) and with the sibling how-much page ($10,801), served live; vs-flat-rate says 800 sq ft overlay vs 1,000 sq ft full-depth is a 'several-times difference in mix tons' (9.67 t vs 20.06 t, about 2.1x); vs-jobnimbus calls the method 'full-depth reclaim' (FDR is in-place pulverizing and stabilizing, which this tool does not model; it models remove-and-replace) and states JobNimbus founders and HQ with no source file, and carries session-meta text ('not reachable from this session') on a public page. JobNimbus is not misrepresented on price (none given).
evidence.fitness: Walked a contractor's job: preset 800 sq ft overlay. The page shows 5.6 'crew hours' and multiplies them by one $38 wage, so total labor is $280 for paving a driveway; a real crew is 4-6 people plus paver and roller operators for half a day or more (roughly 15-30 man-hours). There is no crew-size field, so a contractor typing their real crew-hours and a worker's wage under-prices labor by the crew size; one typing man-hours with the shipped per-sq-ft rates is far below real production. The bid can be made right only by reinterpreting the wage field as an all-hands crew cost, which the page never says.
evidence.domain: Compared against NAPA/state DOT practice: tonnage (145 pcf ~ 109 lb/sy/in vs the 110 rule) is sound, margin-on-price is correct, separate millings and demo dump tickets match practice, tack skipped on new base in full-depth is reasonable. Departures: labor has no crew size (estimators price crew-hours x crew size x loaded wage, or a crew day rate); full-depth prices aggregate only on the failed-base patch, with no fine grading/compaction of base across the whole area; aggregate at 135 pcf is the low end for compacted crushed base (~140-150 pcf). 'Full-depth reclaim' on the JobNimbus page misnames the method.

defects.what: Labor is total hours x one worker's loaded wage with no crew size, while the page labels the hours 'Crew hours' and the wage 'Crew hourly wage'. A contractor entering real crew-hours and a hand's wage under-prices labor by the crew size; the shipped defaults put labor for an 800 sq ft overlay at $280 (5.59 h x $50.16), far below a 4-6 person paving crew's real cost.

Fabric decision page table shows $8,714.45 / $10,619.59 (cost $6,274.40 / $7,646.10) for the fabric preset; the tool shows $8,896.28 / $10,801.42 and the sibling how-much page says $10,801. Its test omits the page's default trip (1.5 h) and site (0.75 h) hours, so it pins the page to numbers the tool never displays. Served live.

Blank fields silently become 0: number('') is 0 and the page passes raw strings, so a cleared wage, mix price or existing depth prices that line at zero (blank mix: $3,076.25 -> $1,440.97) with no warning.
vs-jobnimbus calls the method 'full-depth reclaim'; full-depth reclamation is in-place pulverizing and stabilizing, which this tool does not price (it prices remove, dump and repave).
'several-times difference in mix tons' between the 800 sq ft overlay and the 1,000 sq ft full-depth; the calculator's own figures are 9.67 t vs 20.06 t, about 2x.
JobNimbus founders and headquarters stated with no source in the repo, and public page carries session-meta text ('not reachable from this session').

Full-depth prices aggregate and base hours only on the failed-base patch; no fine grading or compaction of base across the whole replaced area, and 135 pcf is the low end for compacted crushed aggregate.

verdict: The arithmetic is right and well tested: four outputs recomputed independently (tonnage against the NAPA 110 lb/sy/in rule within 1.1%, three full bids to the cent) and all nine seeded mutations were caught. It misses the bar on claims (2): the fabric page's live price table disagrees with the tool by $181.83 because its test copies the defaults without trip and site hours, a comparison page misnames the method as full-depth reclaim, and another overstates a 2x tonnage gap as several-fold. A paving estimator's first check, labor, exposes the larger gap: hours are multiplied by one worker's wage with no crew size, so fitness and domain are 2. Finished (completeness 3), not at the senior-professional bar.
